mainTopic: Neglecting פריה ורביה, the ten-year rule for a childless couple, and the prayers of the infertile אבות
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about how serious it is not to do פריה ורביה. One view says the שכינה rests only on at least 22,000 Jews, so one missing child can make it leave. אבא חנן says such a man deserves death, and אחרים say he leaves the שכינה with no one to rest on. A new משנה then sets a limit: after ten childless years, a man may no longer neglect the מצוה. If he divorces his wife, she may remarry and her new husband gets ten years too. A ברייתא finds a hint for the ten years in אברהם, and teaches that years outside ארץ ישראל, or years of sickness or prison, do not count. רבא asks why we do not learn a twenty-year wait from יצחק. The גמרא answers that יצחק's ages are in the תורה to work out יעקב's age. Then come teachings of רבי יצחק on why the אבות were infertile and on the power of the prayer of צדיקים. The amud ends as רבי אמי begins to prove that אברהם and שרה were טומטמין, a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The שכינה needs at least 22,000 Jews, so one missing child matters
steps.stepSummary: From a פסוק, the ברייתא shows that the שכינה rests only on at least 22,000 Jews. So a man who skips פריה ורביה could be the one who makes the number fall short.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that the שכינה does not rest on fewer than 22,000 Jews. So if Israel were 22,000 minus one, and this man did not have children, he would be the cause of the שכינה leaving Israel!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes reading a פסוק and uses it to show how harmful it is when one man does not have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "thousands" and "ten-thousands" are both plural, so each means at least two: 2,000 plus 20,000. If the nation is exactly one person short, the child this man never had could have completed the number. So his not having children is not just a private matter; it affects the whole nation.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply

steps.confusionAlert: The number 22,000 is not a typo for 2,000 or 20,000. It comes from two thousands (2,000) plus two ten-thousands (20,000).

phrases.english: This teaches that the Divine Presence does not rest

phrases.aramaic: עַל פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנֵי אֲלָפִים וּשְׁנֵי רְבָבוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: upon fewer than two thousands and two ten-thousands of Israel.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is במדבר 10:36, "רבבות אלפי ישראל." Both words are plural, so at least two of each: 22,000.

phrases.english: So if Israel were

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים וּשְׁנֵי רְבָבוֹת חָסֵר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: two thousands and two ten-thousands minus one,
and this man did not engage in being fruitful and multiplying,
is he not found to be causing
the Divine Presence to depart from Israel?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began on the previous page about one who neglects פריה ורביה.
steps.raayaObject: That one who neglects פריה ורביה can cause the שכינה to leave Israel
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural wording of במדבר 10:36, "רבבות אלפי ישראל"

steps.title: אבא חנן: one who does not have children deserves death
steps.stepSummary: אבא חנן, quoting רבי אליעזר, says that one who neglects פריה ורביה is liable to death. He learns it from נדב ואביהוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר: he is liable to death, as it says "and they had no sons." This implies that if they had had sons, they would not have died.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion in the ברייתא gives an even stronger statement: such a man deserves death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about נדב ואביהוא's death adds that they had no children. אבא חנן reads that extra detail as a reason: had they had sons, they would not have died. So having no children is treated as something that makes a person liable to death.

keyTerms.meaning: this implies (that the opposite is true)

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Abba Chanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
He is liable to death,
phrases.notes: "He" is the man who does not do פריה ורביה, the subject of this whole ברייתא.

phrases.english: as it says: "And they had no sons,"
implying that had they had sons,
they would not have died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, harsher view of the same man discussed in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who neglects פריה ורביה is liable to death, learned from נדב ואביהוא.

steps.title: אחרים: without children, there is no one for the שכינה to rest on
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say such a man drives the שכינה away from Israel. The proof is from God's promise to be God to אברהם's offspring after him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: he causes the שכינה to leave Israel, as it says "to be a God to you and to your offspring after you." When there is offspring after you, the שכינה rests. If there is no offspring after you, on whom will it rest? On wood and stones?!
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion explains the harm in a different way: without children, the שכינה has no people to rest on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties God's closeness to the next generation, "your offspring after you." With no children, there would be nobody for the שכינה to dwell among, only wood and stones. Unlike step 1, which depends on an exact count, this view says every missing generation pushes the שכינה away.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others say": an unnamed opinion in a ברייתא
wood and stones, meaning lifeless things

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on neglecting פריה ורביה: it can make the שכינה leave because the 22,000 count falls short; it makes a man liable to death (אבא חנן, from נדב ואביהוא); and it drives away the שכינה because there are no descendants for it to rest on (אחרים).

phrases.english: Others say:
He causes the Divine Presence to depart from Israel,
as it says: "To be a God to you
and to your offspring after you,"
When your offspring is after you,
the Divine Presence rests;
if there is no "offspring after you,"
upon whom will it rest?
Upon the wood and the stones?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason and a different פסוק than אבא חנן in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who neglects פריה ורביה causes the שכינה to leave Israel, since the שכינה rests on future generations.

steps.title: The משנה: ten childless years, the second husband, and miscarriage
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: after ten childless years, a man may no longer neglect the מצוה. If he divorces her, she may remarry and the second husband gets his own ten years. A miscarriage restarts the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man married a woman, stayed with her ten years, and she did not give birth, he may not neglect the מצוה. If he divorced her, she may marry someone else, and the second husband may stay with her ten years. If she miscarried, he counts the ten years from the miscarriage.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and puts the ideas above into practice: it sets a time limit for a couple who have no children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten years is the limit. After that, the husband cannot just keep going without fulfilling פריה ורביה. She is not labeled unable to have children: she may remarry, and the new husband also gets a full ten years. A miscarriage shows she can become pregnant, so the count starts over from then.

keyTerms.meaning: he is not permitted to neglect (the מצוה)

steps.confusionAlert: "Not permitted to neglect" does not say she is the one who cannot have children. The משנה itself lets her marry again, and her second husband gets a fresh ten years.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source of the practical ten-year rule for a couple who have no children.

phrases.english: Mishnah: If he married a woman and stayed with her
ten years and she did not give birth,
he is not permitted to neglect [the מצוה].
If he divorced her,
she is permitted to marry another man.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַשַּׁאי הַשֵּׁנִי לִשְׁהוֹת עִמָּהּ עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: And the second husband may stay with her ten years.
And if she miscarried,
he counts from the time she miscarried.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה וְשָׁהָה עִמָּהּ עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving from the seriousness of the מצוה to a practical time limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After ten childless years, a husband may not keep neglecting פריה ורביה. A divorced wife may remarry and gets a new ten years, and a miscarriage restarts the count.

steps.title: ברייתא: he divorces her and pays her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: after ten childless years, the husband divorces her and pays her כתובה, because maybe he simply did not merit children with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: if a man married a woman, stayed with her ten years, and she did not give birth, he should divorce her and give her the כתובה, for perhaps he did not merit to have children from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that spells out what the husband does after the ten years and adds that she gets her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the משנה's case and adds a money rule: she receives her כתובה. The reason is that we cannot blame her; maybe this couple just was not meant to have children together. This fits the משנה letting her marry again.

keyTerms.meaning: he should send her out (divorce her)
the marriage contract payment owed to the wife
to be built, meaning to have children

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:
If he married a woman and stayed with her
ten years and she did not give birth,
he should divorce her and give her the marriage contract payment,
for perhaps he did not merit to be built from her.
phrases.notes: "Built" here means having children with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא restates the משנה's case and adds that she gets her כתובה, with the reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After ten childless years, he divorces her and pays the כתובה, since the lack of children may not be her fault.

steps.title: A hint for the ten-year rule from אברהם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא admits there is no real proof for the ten-year rule, but brings a hint from אברהם: he took הגר after ten years in ארץ כנען.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no real proof for this, there is a hint: "At the end of ten years of אברם living in ארץ כנען."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 5 gives a hint from the Torah for the ten-year rule. אברהם waited ten childless years with שרה before taking another wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly says this is not a full proof (ראיה), only a hint (זכר). The ten-year rule is a rabbinic number that leans on the story of אברהם. In that פסוק, שרה gives הגר to אברם right after ten years.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint or reminder for the matter, weaker than a proof

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: Although there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter:
"At the end of ten years
of Avram's dwelling in the land of Canaan" —
phrases.notes: בראשית 16:3. In this פסוק שרה gives הגר to אברם as a wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף על פי שאין ראיה לדבר זכר לדבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural hint for the ten-year rule in the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The ten-year waiting period before taking another wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 16:3, אברהם took הגר after ten years in ארץ כנען

steps.title: Years outside the Land, sickness, or prison do not count
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'in the land of Canaan' the ברייתא learns that years outside ארץ ישראל do not count. In the same way, years of sickness or prison do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that living outside the Land does not count toward the ten years. So if he was sick, or she was sick, or both were in prison, those years do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical rule from the same פסוק about which years count toward the ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says אברהם's ten years were 'in the land of Canaan,' so only years in ארץ ישראל count. The idea behind it: years when they could not really expect children are not counted. That is why sickness and prison are left out too.
steps.whatToRemember: Only years in ארץ ישראל when the couple could actually try for children count toward the ten.

phrases.english: to teach you that living outside the Land does not
count toward his tally.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ, חָלָה הוּא אוֹ שֶׁחָלְתָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Therefore, if he was sick or she was sick,
or the two of them were locked in prison —
those years do not count toward his tally.

steps.triggerLanguage: ללמדך שאין ישיבת חוץ לארץ עולה לו מן המנין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further rule from the פסוק brought in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Years outside ארץ ישראל, and years of sickness or imprisonment, are not counted toward the ten years.

steps.title: רבא: why not learn a twenty-year wait from יצחק?
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that יצחק married at forty and had children at sixty. That is twenty years, so why not learn the rule from him?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Let us learn from יצחק! It says יצחק was forty when he married רבקה, and sixty when she gave birth. That is twenty years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the ten-year number. יצחק waited twenty years and did not take another wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אברהם teaches ten years, יצחק seems to teach that waiting longer is fine. Two אבות point to two different numbers, so why choose אברהם's?

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
But let us learn from Yitzchak, as it is written:
"And Yitzchak was forty years old
when he took Rivkah, etc."
and it is written: "And Yitzchak was sixty years old
when she gave birth to them"!
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:26. Sixty minus forty means twenty years of waiting, not ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבא לרב נחמן ולילף מיצחק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source from אברהם by pointing to יצחק.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the ten-year limit from אברהם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יצחק waited twenty years, which suggests a longer wait is allowed.

steps.title: רב נחמן: יצחק was infertile
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that יצחק himself was infertile, so taking another wife would not have helped.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: יצחק was infertile.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains why יצחק is no model for the waiting period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason to take another wife is that maybe the first wife is the cause. יצחק knew the problem was also his, so a new wife would not change anything. That is why he waited.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yitzchak was infertile.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: יצחק's situation was special
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יצחק's twenty years show a longer wait is allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: יצחק was infertile himself, so a second wife would not help; no rule can be learned from him

steps.title: But אברהם was also infertile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: אברהם was also infertile, so the same reasoning should knock out the proof from him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, אברהם was also infertile!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רב נחמן's answer against the source from אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said יצחק did not take another wife because he knew he was infertile himself. But אברהם was also infertile, and he still took הגר after ten years. So being infertile cannot be the reason יצחק waited, and רב נחמן's answer falls.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אַבְרָהָם נָמֵי עָקוּר הָיָה!
phrases.english: If so, Avraham was also infertile!

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הכי אברהם נמי עקור היה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9 by applying it to אברהם.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's distinction between אברהם and יצחק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אברהם was infertile too, so either both can be sources or neither can.

steps.title: יצחק's ages are written to work out יעקב's age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק about יצחק's age is needed for a different teaching. Through the years of ישמעאל, it lets us work out יעקב's age.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed for רבי חייא בר אבא's teaching. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Why does the תורה count ישמעאל's years? To figure out יעקב's years from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we still do not learn a waiting period from יצחק's numbers: those numbers are in the Torah for a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ages of יצחק were written so we can line up dates and work out יעקב's age with the help of ישמעאל's years. Since those numbers have that purpose, they are not a source for how long to wait for children. The פסוק about אברהם, though, ties the ten years directly to taking הגר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
To figure out, to line up (dates)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's words are about ישמעאל's years, not יצחק's. The point is only that the Torah's numbers here are for dating יעקב's life, not for teaching a halacha about waiting.

phrases.english: That verse is needed
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק giving יצחק's age when the twins were born.

phrases.english: for the teaching of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Why were the years of Yishmael counted?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְיַיחֵס בָּהֶן שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: In order to figure out through them the years of Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: ההוא מיבעי ליה לכדרבי חייא בר אבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by showing that the יצחק verses serve a different purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יצחק's ages teach how long a man may wait
steps.terutzMaskana: יצחק's ages are there for dating יעקב's life, so they teach no rule about waiting

steps.title: רבי יצחק proves יצחק was infertile
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק proves from the word לנכח that יצחק and רבקה were both infertile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: יצחק אבינו was infertile, as it says: "יצחק prayed to ה׳ opposite his wife." It does not say "for his wife," but "opposite." This teaches that both of them were infertile.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement gives a source for רב נחמן's claim from step 9 that יצחק was infertile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only רבקה had the problem, the פסוק would say יצחק prayed 'for' (על) his wife. Instead it says 'opposite' (לנכח), as if the two of them stood in the same situation. So both of them needed the prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: And he prayed a lot, begged

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Yitzchak our father was infertile, as it says:
"And Yitzchak prayed to ה׳ opposite his wife."
It does not say "for his wife,"
but "opposite,"
which teaches that both of them were infertile.
phrases.notes: "Opposite" here suggests they matched each other: he had the same problem she did.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יצחק יצחק אבינו עקור היה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of step 9 with a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יצחק and רבקה were both infertile, as shown by the word לנכח.

steps.title: Then why does it say only his prayer was answered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if both were infertile and both prayed, the פסוק should say ה׳ answered 'them,' not 'him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, "and He accepted his prayer" should have said "and He accepted their prayer"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's reading from the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both of them needed help and both were praying, the answer should be to both of them. The singular word 'לו' (to him) seems to show that only יצחק's prayer mattered.

phrases.english: If so, "and He accepted his prayer" —
it should have said "and He accepted their prayer"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הכי ויעתר לו ויעתר להם מיבעי ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק's reading in step 12 from the wording of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that both were infertile and both prayed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses the singular 'to him,' not 'to them.'

steps.title: A righteous son of a righteous father prays more powerfully
steps.stepSummary: The answer: יצחק, a צדיק son of a צדיק, had a stronger prayer than רבקה, a צדקת whose father was wicked. So the answer came because of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the prayer of a righteous person whose father was righteous is not the same as the prayer of a righteous person whose father was wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק says ה׳ answered only יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them prayed, but יצחק's prayer carried more weight because his father אברהם was a צדיק. רבקה's father was wicked. So the Torah credits the answer to יצחק, without saying רבקה was not infertile.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous person whose father was righteous
A righteous person whose father was wicked

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק reads לנכח to mean that both יצחק and רבקה were infertile. ה׳ answered because of יצחק's prayer, since he was a צדיק בן צדיק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes רבי יצחק's reading of the פסוק about יצחק and רבקה. The ten-year rule itself was already defended in step 11: יצחק's ages are in the Torah to work out יעקב's age, so they teach no waiting period.

phrases.english: Because it is not the same:
the prayer of a righteous man, son of a righteous man,
phrases.notes: That is יצחק, son of אברהם.

phrases.english: compared to the prayer of a righteous person, son of a wicked man.
phrases.notes: That is רבקה, whose father בתואל was wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: לפי שאינו דומה תפלת צדיק בן צדיק לתפלת צדיק בן רשע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the singular wording by the different strength of the two prayers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The singular 'לו' shows only יצחק needed or offered prayer
steps.terutzMaskana: Both prayed, but the answer came because of יצחק's stronger prayer as a צדיק בן צדיק

steps.title: Why our forefathers were infertile
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that the אבות were infertile because הקדוש ברוך הוא desires the prayers of צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Why were our forefathers infertile? Because הקדוש ברוך הוא desires the prayers of צדיקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new teaching from רבי יצחק that explains the reason behind the infertility of the אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps showed that the אבות and אמהות were infertile and had to pray. רבי יצחק now explains why. It was not a punishment. הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to hear their prayers, so He held back children until they prayed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the infertility of the אבות from a problem into a purpose: it was the way their prayer was brought out.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
For what reason were our forefathers infertile?
Because the Holy One, Blessed be He,
desires the prayers of the righteous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִפְּנֵי מָה הָיוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עֲקוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the discussion of יצחק and רבקה's infertility and prayer by explaining the purpose of the infertility.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אבות were infertile because הקדוש ברוך הוא desires the prayers of צדיקים.

steps.title: The prayer of the righteous is like a pitchfork
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that the prayer of צדיקים is compared to a pitchfork (עתר) because it turns ה׳'s anger into mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Why is the prayer of צדיקים compared to a pitchfork? A pitchfork turns grain over from one place to another. In the same way, the prayer of צדיקים turns over the ways of הקדוש ברוך הוא, from anger to mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a second teaching about the power of the prayer of צדיקים, based on the word עתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about יצחק's prayer uses the word ויעתר, which sounds like עתר, a pitchfork. A farmer uses a pitchfork to flip grain from one spot to another. רבי יצחק says prayer does the same thing: it flips ה׳'s way of dealing with the world from anger to mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: A pitchfork, used to turn over grain

steps.whatToRemember: The prayer of צדיקים is like a pitchfork: it 'flips' ה׳'s anger into mercy.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלָה תְּפִלָּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כְּעֶתֶר —
phrases.english: Why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork?
phrases.notes: The word ויעתר in the פסוק about יצחק's prayer (בראשית 25:21) sounds like עתר, a pitchfork.

phrases.english: Just as this pitchfork turns over the grain
from place to place,
so the prayer of the righteous

phrases.aramaic: מְהַפֶּכֶת מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: turns over the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
from the attribute of anger to the attribute of mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלָה תְּפִלָּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כְּעֶתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי יצחק on the same theme, the prayer of צדיקים, now explaining its power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prayer of צדיקים turns ה׳'s attribute of anger into the attribute of mercy, like a pitchfork turning over grain.

steps.title: אברהם and שרה were originally טומטמין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says אברהם and שרה were originally טומטמין and begins quoting a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: אברהם and שרה were טומטמין, as it says: "Look to the rock..."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי opens a new teaching about the physical condition of אברהם and שרה. The גמרא starts quoting his proof פסוק, which continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא said the אבות were 'infertile'. רבי אמי goes further: אברהם and שרה were טומטמין, meaning their bodies were closed off and could not produce children at all. The proof from the פסוק has only just started here and will be finished in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: People whose private organs are hidden or closed off
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not complete yet. The פסוק is cut off, and the גמרא will explain how it shows this in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Abraham and Sarah were tumtumin,
phrases.notes: A טומטום is someone whose private organs are covered over, so they cannot have children.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Look to the rock
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 51:1. The פסוק continues in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אַבְרָהָם וְשָׂרָה טוּמְטְמִין הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why the אבות were infertile to a more specific claim about the physical condition of אברהם and שרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם and שרה were originally טומטמין, which will be proven from the פסוק "הביטו אל צור".
